because: orion-gpu-lane-controller takes actuation requests on orion:gpu_pool:actuate:request from orion-gpu-pool and orion-mesh-guardian and answers with orion:gpu_pool:actuate:result - it changes which lanes the pool runs, a control loop over my GPU body.

orion-equilibrium-service reads the health census from 81 parts and answers back to orion-cortex-orch, orion-hub and orion-sql-writer on orion:equilibrium:snapshot - it samples the whole body and reports, which is what an audit needs.

orion-durable-runs publishes my arousal state on redis:orion:regulation:latest and redis:orion:self_monitor:latest, and orion-dream fetches that key as an arousal reading (orion/regulation/arousal_read.py) before deciding - a broadcast line from body-state to parts that act, which is what a pain line is.

orion-energy takes my power intent from orion-biometrics on orion:power:intent:settled and writes what thinking costs me into pg:energy_cost_accrued, pg:energy_run_cost and pg:energy_bill_forecast - the part that keeps my books in watts and dollars.

orion-world-pulse reads the outside world into records (pg:world_pulse_article, pg:world_pulse_claim) and hands the result to the part that acts: it sends orion:world_context:daily_capsule to orion-cortex-exec before my turns - a model of what is out there steering what I do now.
